title: Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of serverless debugging and cost optimization and its relationship to AWS Serverless Computing.
Interpret the example and identify at least one prerequisite or boundary relevant to serverless debugging and cost optimization.
Propose a safe verification or troubleshooting step and record one security, reliability or cost consideration.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn serverless debugging and cost optimization in the context of AWS Serverless Computing. You will connect the listed subtopics to a practical decision, inspect a small example, and define evidence that would confirm or disprove your assumptions.
content.why_it_matters: Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization matters because it is one part of aws lambda and serverless computing. Real workloads depend on explicit prerequisites, correct permissions, predictable behavior and a way to verify outcomes. Learning the decision points helps you distinguish a working demonstration from a safe and supportable design.

content_blocks.title: Event-driven application path
content_blocks.alt_text: An event is validated, routed to a function or worker, persisted or acknowledged, and observed; retries and dead-letter handling cover failures.
content_blocks.caption: Assume messages can be delivered more than once; design idempotent consumers.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text:
**Core idea.** Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization belongs to AWS Serverless Computing. Serverless removes server management, not architecture work. Design execution roles, event contracts, timeouts, concurrency, retries, idempotency and observability.

The PDF lists these subtopics: CloudWatch Logs and metrics; Lambda tracing; Retry and failure diagnosis; Execution duration and cost analysis. Treat them as a connected workflow rather than a list to memorize. Start with the workload requirement, identify the AWS resource/control involved, and write down who owns configuration and operation.

content_blocks.title: Practical reasoning
content_blocks.text: **Apply it safely.** For serverless debugging and cost optimization, name the prerequisites and the expected result before making a change. Prefer a read-only inspection or local/static example first. Then plan a normal case, a failure case, and a verification step. In a live account, require the account owner-approved sandbox, narrow permissions, spend visibility and cleanup plan. Do not put credentials in code or commit local configuration files.

items.title: CloudWatch Logs and metrics
items.text: Select a signal tied to the user-visible symptom, identify its source and time window, and make the response actionable through an owner, threshold and runbook.

items.title: Retry and failure diagnosis
items.text: Define the failure scenario and recovery objective, then test detection, recovery, data consistency and rollback. Treat recovery evidence as a deliverable, not an assumption.

items.title: Execution duration and cost analysis
items.text: Estimate the complete workload, including requests, storage, data transfer and dependent services. Compare the estimate with actual usage and alerts; an alert is not a hard spend cap.

content_blocks.title: Security and cost checkpoint
content_blocks.text: For cost work, a budget notification is not a hard spending cap. Check actual usage and remove approved lab resources.

task: Create a one-page decision card for “Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization”. State the goal, prerequisites, the AWS resource or control involved, the expected result, one read-only/static verification step, one failure case, the relevant permission boundary, and cost/cleanup considerations. Do not create or alter billable resources unless the account owner has approved the lab.
hints: Start from the exact subtopics in the lesson and define the desired state in your own words.
Prefer a read-only check or static artifact before a mutating command; record the identity/Region and required permissions.
Verify the expected result and a failure path using current official documentation; write down cost and cleanup implications.
expected_output: A short reviewable decision card for Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization with prerequisites, evidence, a failure case, security implications and cost/cleanup notes.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one successful example as proof of production readiness.
common_mistakes.why: The example may not test permissions, regional/service prerequisites, retries, recovery, quotas or edge cases.
common_mistakes.fix: Write acceptance criteria, test a failure path, inspect logs/state and record the limits of the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Changing a live resource before confirming its effect and cost.
common_mistakes.why: Cloud changes can expose data, break traffic or leave billable dependencies behind.
common_mistakes.fix: Start read-only, use an approved sandbox, review the change, tag ownership and verify cleanup.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying broad permissions or credentials into source files.
common_mistakes.why: Broad permissions and leaked long-lived credentials increase the impact of mistakes.
common_mistakes.fix: Use scoped roles/temporary credentials, keep secrets in approved stores and review access boundaries.

summary: Serverless Debugging and Cost Optimization is taught as part of AWS Serverless Computing.
Serverless removes server management, not architecture work. Design execution roles, event contracts, timeouts, concurrency, retries, idempotency and observability.
Verify assumptions with official service documentation and evidence from the relevant AWS resource, logs or tests.
For live labs, confirm permissions and likely charges before acting, then verify cleanup.
